title: Corporate Digital Responsibility and Sustainable Consumer Behaviour Toward Global Technology Platforms in Bangladesh: A Stakeholder-Centred Research Model
content: This study develops a stakeholder-centred explanation of how corporate digital responsibility (CDR) may relate to sustainable consumer behaviour in the context of global technology platforms in Bangladesh. Unlike group papers centred on adoption intention, privacy concern, trust or AI transparency, this article focuses on the responsibility-to-behaviour pathway: whether perceived responsible digital conduct is associated with consumers’ evaluation of firms’ obligations to users and society and with preferences for digital services that demonstrate socially responsible practices. The research plan specifies a quantitative, cross-sectional survey, a five-point Likert instrument, purposive eligibility screening and a target of 400 responses, with at least 385 usable cases. Stakeholder Theory, the Corporate Digital Responsibility framework and the Theory of Planned Behavior provide complementary conceptual lenses. The supplied workbook contains 385 populated records with complete values for the nine focal items. Exploratory composite means were 4.12 for CDR, 4.18 for perceived stakeholder responsibility (PSR), and 3.78 for sustainable consumer behaviour (SCB). However, preliminary Cronbach’s alpha estimates were only 0.33, 0.31, and 0.42, respectively, indicating that the current item sets do not demonstrate acceptable internal consistency. Simple regression diagnostics show positive associations, but these estimates are not treated as confirmatory hypothesis tests because measurement quality and data provenance remain unresolved. The paper therefore contributes a distinctive, testable framework and a transparent analysis pathway, while identifying the specific validation work required before empirical claims can be advanced.
